title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Oct 2026) — 10:00 ET, the buy-side positioning read whose panel answers across the September FOMC minutes and which prints the day before CPI
source: EST: DERIVED BY RULE — the publisher states no date for this series and none can be read. S&P Global's PMI calendar (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 with browser headers, HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) is a ROLLING ~4-WEEK WINDOW: today it runs 'September 11' to 'October 07' and lists the IMI exactly once, on September 15. Its 'standard monthly release schedules' block names rules for the Manufacturing, Services and Whole Economy PMIs and NO rule for the IMI; the August 2026 release PDF was re-read this session and carries no 'next release' line either. So the October date is a rule output. The rule — the Tuesday EIGHT DAYS AFTER the month's first Monday — was fitted by the sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-09-15 lane on three 2026 mastheads and is EXTENDED HERE TO SIX PRIMARY MASTHEADS ACROSS THREE YEARS, three of them fetched direct this session: 2024-03-12 (hash f8dd3961…, HTTP 200, 387,805 B, 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 12 March 2024'; first Monday 2024-03-04), 2025-10-14 (c7973bae…, 200, 219,989 B, '1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 14 October 2025'; first Monday 2025-10-06) and 2026-06-09 (b9201952…, 200, 401,271 B, '1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 9 June 2026'; first Monday 2026-06-01), joining the parent's 2026-01-13, 2026-05-12 and 2026-08-11 and the listed 2026-09-15. SEVEN FOR SEVEN. The decisive one is 2025-10-14: the same MONTH and the same holiday geometry as this entry — Columbus Day fell on the second Monday (2025-10-13) and the release was the Tuesday after it, exactly as 2026-10-12 / 2026-10-13 would be. October 2026's first Monday is 2026-10-05, giving 2026-10-13; 14:00 UTC = 10:00 ET under EDT (DST does not end until 2026-11-01). Filed estimate for ONE honest reason and not the one prior lanes gave: no publisher statement of this date exists, anywhere, so it cannot be confirmed however good the arithmetic is. The 'no confirmed prefix covers a private survey compiler' reason five IMI/PMI lanes have cited is CONTESTED IN THIS REPO'S OWN PRACTICE — existing-home-sales-2026-10-13 (NAR) and challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03 (Challenger, Gray & Christmas) both carry IR: for exactly this class — but it does not bind here, because this lane has no primary source to attach a prefix to. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this id's own never-assessed initial research, from the single proposal that existed (…from-sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-09-15.json, now inert). NOT A TRADE: symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook targets it, no consensus is published for a sentiment survey so no surprise is testable, and the date is estimate — an estimate widens caution and never licenses an entry. THREE STRUCTURAL FACTS THAT MAKE THIS EDITION DIFFERENT FROM THE SEPTEMBER ONE. (1) The 10:00 ET slot is SHARED, not clean: existing-home-sales-2026-10-13 (confirmed, IR:, 10:00 a.m. ET) sits in it. That confound is sized and small — its own ledger measures 114 EHS release days over 2,514 sessions leaving SPY at p=0.66, ITB p=0.58, XHB p=0.45 — so attribution is degraded rather than hopeless, unlike the manufacturing sibling's 10-01 ISM collision. (2) The field window, forced by the rule into the week of 2026-10-05, contains the SEPTEMBER FOMC MINUTES (2026-10-07, 14:00 ET) — the first time a Fed communication lands inside an IMI panel's own collection window in any edition this lane has read. Whether it does depends on Wednesday-vs-Thursday close and is printed on the release. (3) It lands the day BEFORE September CPI (2026-10-14) and 15 days before a 10-28 FOMC that has NO SEP, where the September edition landed the morning before a dot plot. Tape verdict inherited and STRENGTHENED, not assumed: this session measured 32 rule-derived release days 2024-2026 at daily resolution and found SPY p=0.85, QQQ p=0.38, TLT p=0.24 and ^TNX p=0.64 against all other sessions; the one hit (IWM p=0.005, QUIETER not louder) is matched by a placebo at the same rate — a first-Monday+k sweep over k=1..14 returns exactly one other p<0.05, SPY at k=10. Next edition derived by the same rule: 2026-11-10, proposed in this PR, which would land ON CPI day.
